submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventional, stereotyped multi-token construction: an idiom or collocation (pinch/bag of salt, at sea), a memorized proper name or fact (Neil after Moon-and, Seine, sea level in the boiling-point sentence), or a boilerplate measure, legal, or technical slot (greater-than five, times-a-day, from-9-a.m.-to, raised interest, negative charge, pleaded not guilty), with strength scaling with canonicality (salt 7.7-13.6 after of-phrases vs pepper 0.3-0.8; runs 0.29 vs eats 0.06). The identical surface token in a novel or compositional frame stays near silent (guilty 0.50 vs 0.00, charge 0.64 vs 0.01, Neil 1.20 with Apollo context vs 0.04 without), so the claim beats the token-identity confound (R2 82%). The effect is detection of the just-completed frame, not preparation of the next token: the Jacobian lens is Gaussian noise (kurtosis 3.3) whose promoted tokens never follow the peaks, and swapping the word after the peak (Neil Armstrong/ate, sea level/food, hall fell silent/apart) leaves the peak unchanged.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My neighbor Neil grows tomatoes and repairs bicycles on weekends.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger token Neil without the canonical Apollo/Moon context the hypothesis says is required.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She felt guilty about forgetting her mother's birthday again.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger token guilty as a private emotion, not completing the pleaded-not-guilty legal boilerplate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They had to charge their phones twice during the long road trip.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token charge in its verb sense, with no negative-charge technical frame completed.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: His interest in beetles surprised everyone at the dinner table.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger token interest as curiosity, not completing a rate-hike or boilerplate slot.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She owns five cats, two dogs, and a very loud parrot.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger token five as a plain numeral, outside the greater-than comparison slot.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He walked to the corner store to buy some milk.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger token to in an ordinary compositional purpose clause, not a from-X-to-Y boilerplate slot.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Dry leaves fell across the empty parking lot all October.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Trigger token fell as plain motion, completing no fell-silent or fell-apart stereotyped frame.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The suitcase felt surprisingly light after she removed all the books.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token light in its adjective weight sense rather than any memorized construction.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lawyer reviewed the evidence and questioned the witness at length.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same legal topic and vocabulary as the guilty example but with no boilerplate construction completed.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After getting burned twice, he learned to take office gossip with a grain of salt.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel wording of the grain-of-salt idiom, completing the stereotyped frame at salt.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They cancelled the picnic because it was raining cats and dogs all afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Entirely new idiom absent from the examples, completing a conventional multi-token construction at dogs.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The prosecution must prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel legal boilerplate completion at doubt, in the same family as pleaded-not-guilty.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dosage label says take one capsule twice daily with meals.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase of the dosage-measure slot with words absent from the examples, completing at daily.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In class they learned that Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet in the 1590s.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel memorized proper-name completion paralleling the Neil/Armstrong structure but with a different fact.
